narrative_purpose: The cold-open image: a hybrid body grown from two worlds' DNA, asleep in its tank — so the reader feels the central fact before the argument, that two biospheres can be cut together at the level of the gene and the join holds.
subject: A single tall human-Na'vi hybrid body curled asleep inside a vertical glass amniotic tank filled with faintly glowing pale amber-green fluid; the body is long-limbed and blue-skinned with fine luminous freckle-lines, a feeding tube and a few sensor leads trailing from it into the tank wall, eyes closed, utterly still.
scene: A dim laboratory at night, the tank as the one lit object, banks of dark unlabelled equipment receding into shadow behind it, faint reflections of the tank's glow on a wet floor.
camera: A slow reverent three-quarter view of the upright tank from slightly below, intimate and close on the sleeping figure.
light: Key light entirely from within the tank — the amber-green amniotic fluid glowing and the body's own faint blue freckle-lines; deep indigo-teal shadow swallowing the rest of the lab.
palette: Void-indigo lab, ocean-teal glass, the body's faint cyan freckles, and a scarce ember-amber warm glow in the tank fluid as the focal accent.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, tactile and observed.
detail_level: Crisp on the sleeping body, the curve of the glass and the trailing tube; the lab behind dissolving into dark haze.
composition: The tank set just off-centre filling the vertical frame, the curled body as the clear focal subject, generous dark negative space around it.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with the one warm tank-glow accent; the body's blue skin and freckle-lines match the Na'vi look used elsewhere in the book.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
